```{r}
library(lava)
```

```{r}
set.seed(4242)
sim1 <- function(n=1000) {
  w <- rnorm(n)
  a <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.5)
  y <- cos(w) + w*a + w ** 2 + a + rnorm(n)
  data.frame(y, a, w)
}
d <- sim1(n = 500)
```

# Exercise 1 - ANOVA and ANCOVA

## 1.1a ANOVA

Implement the ANOVA estimator for $\psi = E[Y(1)] - E[Y(0)]$ with `lava::estimate`

```{r}

lava_estimate_anova <- function(data, trt) {

  # participants should only implement this part
  theta <- with(data, mean(y[a == trt]))
  ic <- with(data, (a == trt) * (y - theta) / mean(a == trt))
  # up until here

  estimate(
    coef = theta, IC = ic, labels = paste0("E[Y(", trt, ")"), id = TRUE
  )
}

est0 <- lava_estimate_anova(data = d, trt = 0)
est1 <- lava_estimate_anova(data = d, trt = 1)

# perhaps they should implement the constrast themselves
est_anova <- c(
  est0, est1, psi = est1 - est0
)
est_anova
```

## 1.1b ANOVA

Estimate a linear model with response variable y, an intercept and treatment
variable only. Provide the obtained object as the first argument to
`lava::estimate`. Compare the output with the estimator from 1.1a. What do you
observe?

```{r}
fit_unadj <- lm(y ~ a, data = d)
estimate(fit_unadj)
```

## 1.1c Obtain $E[Y(1)]$ from lm fit (optional)

```{r}
est_lm <- estimate(fit_unadj, labels = c("E[Y(0)]", "psi"))
c(est_lm, c("E[Y(1)]" = est_lm["psi"] + est_lm["E[Y(0)]"]))
```

## 1.2a ANCOVA

Implement the ANCOVA estimator for $\psi = E[Y(1)] - E[Y(0)]$ with the
`lava::estimate` function. Adjust for baseline covariate `w`. Use `lm` to fit
the working model `E[Y | A = a,  W] = \alpha_a + \beta W`.

```{r}

lava_estimate_ancova <- function(data, beta, trt) {
  w_bar <- mean(data$w)
  wa_bar <- mean(data$w[data$a == trt])
  pia <- mean(data$a == trt)

  # participants should only implement this part
  theta_unadj <- mean(data$y[data$a == trt])
  theta <- theta_unadj - beta * (wa_bar - w_bar)

  ic0 <- with(
    data,
    (a == trt) * y / pia
  )
  ic1 <- with(data, ((a == trt) - pia) / pia * (theta + beta * (w - w_bar)))
  ic <- ic0 - ic1 - theta
  # up until here

  estimate(
    coef = theta, IC = ic, id = TRUE, labels = paste0("E[Y(", trt, ")")
  )
}

# provided to partipants
fit <- lm(y ~ a + w, data = d)
betahat <- coef(fit)[["w"]]
est0_ancova <- lava_estimate_ancova(data = d, beta = betahat, trt = 0)
est1_ancova <- lava_estimate_ancova(data = d, beta = betahat, trt = 1)
# up until here because they should implement the estimator for the contrast themselves

est_ancova <- c(
  est0_ancova, est1_ancova,  psi = est1_ancova - est0_ancova
)
est_ancova
```

# Exercise 2 - ANHECOVA

## 2.1 ANHECOVA estimator

Implement the ANHECOVA estimator for $\psi = E[Y(1)] - E[Y(0)]$ with the
`lava::estimate` function. Adjust for baseline covariate `w`. Use `lm` to fit
the working model `E[Y | A = a,  W] = \alpha_a + \beta W`.


```{r}
# participants should do everything in this exercise. I think this should be
# a nice way to test their understanding of ANHECOVA
fit_anhecova <- lm(y ~ a * w, data = d)
beta0 <- coef(fit_anhecova)[["w"]]
beta1 <- beta0 + coef(fit_anhecova)[["a:w"]]

est0_anhecova <- lava_estimate_ancova(data = d, beta = beta0, trt = 0)
est1_anhecova <- lava_estimate_ancova(data = d, beta = beta1, trt = 1)

est_anhecova <- c(
  est0_anhecova, est1_anhecova, psi = est1_anhecova - est0_anhecova
)
est_anhecova
```

## 2.2 Comparing all estimators - single data sample

Implement each estimator in single function which accepts a `data` argument and returns a `lava::estimate` object for the treatment effect estimate (i.e. the target parameter)

```{r}
estimator_anova <- function(data) {
  # write the implementation here for est
  # use the results from the first exercise session

  # we just relabel the estimate object
  return(estimate(est, labels = "psi.anova"))
}

estimator_ancova <- function(data) {
  # write the implementation here

  return(estimate(est, labels = "psi.ancova"))
}

estimator_anhecova <- function(data) {
  # write the implementation here

  return(estimate(est, labels = "psi.anhecova"))
}
```

```{r}
estimator_anova <- function(data) {
  est0 <- lava_estimate_anova(data = data, trt = 0)
  est1 <- lava_estimate_anova(data = data, trt = 1)
  est <- est1 - est0

  return(estimate(est, labels = "psi.anova"))
}

estimator_ancova <- function(data) {

  # provided to partipants
  fit <- lm(y ~ a + w, data = data)
  betahat <- coef(fit)[["w"]]
  est0_ancova <- lava_estimate_ancova(data = data, beta = betahat, trt = 0)
  est1_ancova <- lava_estimate_ancova(data = data, beta = betahat, trt = 1)

  est <- est1_ancova - est0_ancova

  return(estimate(est, labels = "psi.ancova"))
}

estimator_anhecova <- function(data) {

  fit_anhecova <- lm(y ~ a * w, data = data)
  beta0 <- coef(fit_anhecova)[["w"]]
  beta1 <- beta0 + coef(fit_anhecova)[["a:w"]]

  est0_anhecova <- lava_estimate_ancova(data = data, beta = beta0, trt = 0)
  est1_anhecova <- lava_estimate_ancova(data = data, beta = beta1, trt = 1)
  est <- est1_anhecova - est0_anhecova

  return(estimate(est, labels = "psi.anhecova"))
}
```

```{r}
c(
  estimator_anova(data = d),
  estimator_ancova(data = d),
  estimator_anhecova(data = d)
)
```

## 2.3 Comparing all estimators - Monte-Carlo simulations

```{r}
onerun <- function(n) {
  d <- sim1(n)
  c(
    estimator_anova(data = d),
    estimator_ancova(data = d),
    estimator_anhecova(data = d)
  )
}

set.seed(42)
res <- sim(onerun, R = 1000, args = list(n = 200),
           mc.cores = parallel::detectCores(), seed = 42)
```

```{r}
summary(res, true = 1)
```
